title: Microsoft is giving Copilot more control over Windows and your files
key_facts: At Microsoft's Windows and Surface event (7 Oct 2026), Microsoft showed an upgrade to Copilot that gets access to local files on a PC and can take actions across the operating system.
The approach is called 'Hybrid Intelligence': apps and tools mix AI models that run locally on the PC with cloud AI models.
Onstage video demo: Microsoft's Autopilot tool searched folders for tax documents, renamed them, zipped them and drafted an email to the accountant with the zip attached.
Jacob Andreou, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, said the Hybrid Intelligence features come to Copilot over the 'next couple months'.
The article reports no independent test and no date for the features beyond 'the next couple months'.
quote_evidence: At today’s Windows and Surface event, Microsoft showed off an upgrade to its Copilot AI system that will give it access to local files on your PC and the ability to take actions across the OS.
Features powered by Hybrid Intelligence will be coming to Copilot over the “next couple months,” Andreou said.
why_it_matters_hint: Windows users who switch the feature on would let Copilot reach local files; so far the evidence is one video demo.
